question.text: The aggregation model in financial advisory refers to:

answer.text: A single adviser managing all aspects of a client's finances
An entity with several distributors who take a range of financial products to clients using shared research and platforms
Government aggregation of all financial data of citizens
Combining all investments into a single mutual fund scheme

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 30 of the workbook describes the aggregation model as an aggregating entity that has several associated distributors taking a range of financial products to clients, with shortlisted products, central research/advisory support, execution platforms, CRM software, and shared facilities. The Trap: This is a description of a distribution business model — it is not about consolidating a client's investments into one scheme, nor about a single adviser handling everything. Note: The defining features are the shared product shortlist, central research, common execution platforms, and shared CRM/facilities across the associated distributors.
